content.title: Masters 2026 is over. Where are the sites for golf's next majors?
content.text: PGAPGA Championship at Aronimink is next on the tee for golf's majors Garry SmitsJacksonville Florida Times-UnionApril 12, 2026Updated April 13, 2026, 10:23 a.m. ETKeep Watching8AUGUSTA, Ga. | The 2026 Masters Tournament is in the books with Rory McIlroy winning his second green jacket in a row by one shot over Scottie Scheffler in a dramatic battle between the two men who have combined to win four of the last five at the Augusta National Golf Club.Who's next on the tee among major championships?The Masters kicked off a four-month stretch in which there is one major championship per month through July. The Players Championship, the PGA Tour's marquee event, was held March 12-15, with Cameron Young winning.Where are the rest of golf's major championships?PGA Championship: May 14-17 at the Aronimink Golf Club in Newton Square, Pa., near Philadelphia. Defending champion: Scheffler. Last major winner at Aronimink: Gary Player, 1962 PGA.Need a news break? Check out the all new PLAY hub with puzzles, games and more!U.S. Open: June 18-21 at the Shinnecock Hills Golf Club in Southampton, N.Y. Defending champion: J.J. Spaun. Last major winner at Shinnecock: Brooks Koepka, 2018 U.S. Open.British Open: July 16-19 at Royal Birkdale, in Southport, England. Defending champion: Scheffler.
